chapter_theme: The Lord is within and pervades everything 'like oil in sesame', so the search outside, in temple tanks, copper images and water rites, is folly, and even moral failing does not bar one who can join him inside. The chapter builds its theology by negation (not standing, not sitting, not bond, not release; cannot be grasped, cannot be told) and by the geometry of the root centre, where the mantra contracts to one letter in which five crore mantras are held. Nearly half the verses end in the refrain விளைந்ததே or அமைந்ததே சிவாயமே.
structure_note: No commentary orders the chapter. Verses of pervasion (1242 to 1245, 1255, 1259) alternate with attacks on water rites and image worship (1246, 1247, 1249, 1252), and verses on the unsayable (1253, 1257, 1258) lead to the letter verses (1248, 1250, 1251, 1262, 1263). 1240 repeats its second line as its fourth.

1239.reading: Even if you kill one creature with another and make it your food, even if in the market you lie, steal and do other wrongs, if you can lovingly join the Lord whom the boar sought, that very day know the gods within yourselves.
1239.nuance: பன்றி தேடும் ஈசன் is the Lord whose foot Vishnu as a boar dug to find. Read plainly the verse makes joining him override the whole moral catalogue; read more softly it says that even sinners are not shut out. The editors' gloss takes மன்று as the market.

1240.reading: If you can stay inside that house and teach knowledge to the breath that rides within the fish-house and speaks maya, the desireless Lord stands as everything; after staying in that house and teaching it knowledge.
1240.nuance: மச்சகம் is obscure: 'fish-house' (மச்சம்), perhaps the body or mind in its waters, or மச்சு, the upper storey, the head. வாயு is the breath, or வாய் the mouth, that talks maya. Line 4 repeats line 2 with a variant (அறுவுணர்த்தி for அறிவுணர்த்தி), so the unit may be damaged.

1241.reading: Like paddy that sprouted in the field being pulled as a weed: if people of the world speak the truth, how are they to survive? Apart from the truth that springs up in the heat of longing, all is false, and the land, born into hell, has suffered its suffering.
1241.nuance: The editors' gloss reads விரகு as the heat of longing; the word also means cunning, giving 'the truth sprung from cunning is only falsehood'. Either way the image is of true speech uprooted like a weed among the crop, and the world called hell.

1242.reading: Sinners who seek the dancing Lord here and there, you do not discern the one who is clear; the thief who stands mingled in forest, land, house and void: run seeking within yourselves, look with love and realise him.
1242.nuance: கள்வன், the thief, is the hidden Lord; the pilgrimage 'here and there' is answered by a seeking turned inward.

1243.reading: The assembly of the dancing celestials, the beyond and the here, the four Vedas that seek, the three gods, the long-living elements, the states in which you stand: without the one who dances, none of it is, none at all.
1243.nuance: ஆடுவாழின் ஒழியலாது is unclear: 'if the dancing one ceases' or 'apart from the one who dances'. On either reading everything listed, Vedas and gods included, depends on the dance.

1244.reading: Becoming is within the Supreme and perishing is within the Supreme; going and entering are within the Supreme; the gods and the directions are within the Supreme; everyone is within the Supreme, and I too am within that Supreme.
1244.nuance: பரம் (the Supreme) is used without a name. The last word, யானும், places the speaker inside what he describes rather than before it.

1245.reading: The seven earths, seven seas, eight places with their mountains, the surrounding sky, the ring of hills and the seven worlds they speak of, the ocean-Mal, the sky-holding great egg and egg upon egg: all rise within the light of the one of the aeon and at once dissolve.
1245.nuance: ஊழியான், the one of the aeon, is the Lord who outlasts the cycles that end in ஊழி. The whole Puranic cosmography is listed in order to be dissolved in one light.

1246.reading: You draw water from the pond; why do your hands tire and stop? You men without wisdom and without a drop of moisture in the mind: if with moisture in the mind you can cut away the dirt, are not the light you thought of and you and I one?
1246.nuance: ஈரம் is wetness and also tenderness: the outer water of the rite is set against the inner moisture of compassion. The last line may address the hearers or the Lord; 'you and I' then means the light, the Lord and the speaker.

1247.reading: Born from water, you perform water rites; thinking of whom do you pour away all that water for nothing? If you can think of the root, the seed and the glory that sprouts from the seed, you will reach Siva's state.
1247.nuance: நீரிலே பிறந்து, born in or from water, points to the seed of 1213: a creature made of water bathing in water gets nowhere. Root and seed are the source of birth and of the self at once.

1248.reading: In the ten matched doorways the root letter spreads; it is the root that moves as the pairing of release and siddhi; the dance that is the great hand of the five mad senses: in the people of the bone-city it was set in place, Sivayam.
1248.nuance: பத்தொடொத்த வாசல் is read as the ten gates of the body (nine openings and the crown) or the ten channels; மூலவக்கரம் is the root letter, the seed mantra. அத்தியூரர் may be the people of a shrine called Atthiyur or, by the pun of 1211 (அஸ்தி, bone), the dwellers in the body. மாகரம் is unclear.

1249.reading: If you hold within you, as your own nature, the measureless light that is atom and cosmos, that is release; instead you mutter 'muna muna' inside, pressing your fingers together, and bewilder yourselves day after day doing worship to copper.
1249.nuance: செம்பு is the copper of the image. விரலை ஒன்றி is counting japa on the fingers or holding finger seals. அணுவினோடும் அண்டமாய், atom and cosmos, is the Siddhars' pairing of the minute and the whole without the compound அண்டபிண்டம்.

1250.reading: Before one faces the root letter, all is folly covered in folly; what folly is this, fools? If the five elements, which are death, contract into the five, does one join the temple, or join the Beginningless?
1250.nuance: ஆலயோடு is probably ஆலயத்தோடு, the temple, shortened for the metre, though ஆல் could be the banyan; the rhetorical answer is the Beginningless. காலனான அஞ்சுபூதம் makes the elements themselves death; their contraction 'into the five' is the dissolution of the gross body. The text has a stray mark before முடரே.

1251.reading: Being the root as the three-cornered figure and also the end, as one; becoming that square and contracting into a single letter; as the lamp of knowledge that shines within the body, the true square: the truth of the mantra one utters is Sivayam.
1251.nuance: The geometry of 1217 again: the triangle at the root contracts to one letter. மெய்ச்சதுரம் makes the body itself the 'true square', the shrine in which the lamp burns; the one letter is taken by tradition as Om or சி.

1252.reading: You do not cut away the dirt of the mind; like earrings you dip yourselves in the tank. Of old your own four-faced one flew about seeking and could not find him; those who see will find him mingled within you, look.
1252.nuance: Brahma flew as a swan seeking Siva's head and failed. வண்டுலங்கள் and குண்டலங்கள் (beetles? earrings) are chosen for rhyme and their sense is loose; the point is the tank-dip without a cleaned mind.

1253.reading: It is not standing and not sitting, not slender and not thick; not bond and not release, free of all conceiving; not smell and not hearing; in the imperishable sky, how is one to speak of the one that stands without end?
1253.nuance: The negations include release as well as bond, so the verse places the Lord beyond the Saiva pair itself. கேடிலாத வான், the imperishable sky, is where it stands, and the question of how to speak of it is left open.

1254.reading: The reason that the fitting water entered and stood within you; you do not discern the One that two bulls bore as a calf; you do not know the cow that is dying beside you; what guise is this, in which the guru dwells and roams?
1254.nuance: Cipher. 'Two bulls bore a calf' is read by tradition as the two parents or the two breaths producing the one; ஆ, the cow, is the soul (பசு) and perhaps the body dying at hand; the 'fitting water' is the seed. The last line can be the Lord wandering in the guru's guise, or a rebuke to one who wears a guru's guise without knowing these things.

1255.reading: Are you not the five letters that dance in the sky? Are you not the supreme consciousness that stands spread out as sparks? Since our Lord is the one enjoyment of every life, our Lord and I stood as one: Sivayam.
1255.nuance: அம்பரம் is the sky and also echoes அம்பலம், the hall; சிம்புகள், sparks or fragments, is the one consciousness scattered as many. ஏகபோகம், the single enjoyment, is union.

1256.reading: The moon with twin lights is the Supreme that moved and stood; the moon with beautiful light, that none of you know; the Supreme that passed beyond the dark-lit veil; the garland-lit great state is the foot of the one Lord.
1256.nuance: The meaning turns on the moons. ஈரொளிய திங்கள், the twin-lit moon, is taken by tradition as the moon that shines with the sun's light and its own, or as the inner moon at the crown fed by the two channels; காரொளிப் படலம், the dark veil, as maya. None of this is said in the verse.

1257.reading: It cannot be grasped, cannot be softened, cannot be chewed in the mouth; cannot be pushed away, cannot be approached, and so within the mind it cannot be settled, cannot be made clear; the inner fruit of the supreme consciousness cannot be split open: how am I to tell of it?
1257.nuance: A string of negative verbs ending in ஒணாது; குதட்டு, to chew, treats the thing as a fruit that the mouth cannot work on, which the next line names the inner fruit.

1258.reading: By speech, by mind, by the reasoning one judges with, thinking on the look that cannot be looked at, who looks at the look? If the unlookable look comes, and one looks and looks and looks, the unlookable look comes and looks at the look where we are.
1258.nuance: நோக்கு, the gaze, is repeated until the subject and object swap: the seer cannot be seen by the seeing, but when the unseeable sight arrives it looks back at the one looking. The verse completes 1226's eye that cannot see itself.

1259.reading: Within and without, spread through the whole world, standing like oil in sesame, our Lord who moves everything: after he softly came and entered me and performed true tapas, what giver is like this giver, and what colour is his colour?
1259.nuance: It is the Lord who does the tapas, inside the poet, which reverses the usual direction of practice. வண்ணம் என்ன வண்ணம் asks what nature a pervading thing can have.

1260.reading: I have seen no Veda, since I have no burning birth; you became the form in which knowledge stands and became all the worlds; as light within the light, with turiya and the state beyond, the primal root became the first: Sivayam.
1260.nuance: வெம்பிறப்பு இலாமையால்: having no hot birth to escape, the poet has no use for a Veda. துரியம் and அதீதம் are the fourth and the beyond-fourth states, named here as where the Lord stands.

1261.reading: Within the fallen knot, twice a span long, you cherish that city and are born and die and wander in it; if you can renounce and cut off the five who are the boat, seeing the small measure you mingle as crores: Sivayam.
1261.nuance: The opening is coded. A plain reading takes சாண் இரு மடங்கு ... சரிந்த கொண்டை as a woman's body and the 'city' as the womb of desire into which men are born again; another takes it as the crown of the head two spans up, the city of the Lord. தோணியான ஐவர், the five who are the boat, are the senses that carry one and must be left; காணி, a small land measure, grows to crores.

1262.reading: If five crore mantras are held within the five, then, to say it in the heart, within you, in the one letter that is thought; if the five, the four and the three become one and are held within you, the five became a single letter: Sivayam.
1262.nuance: A contraction: all mantras into the five letters, the five with the four- and three-letter forms into one letter, which tradition takes as Om or சி. The holding is 'within you', so the reduction is also an interiorisation.

1263.reading: The letter hidden within the letter, the letter hidden inside that; ... in the wheel ...; like oil hidden in sesame, our Lord hides within every letter and stands: who can see this rightness?
1263.nuance: Line 2 (சிவ்வைருண்டு சம்புளத் திருந்ததும்) is garbled and is left untranslated. The frame is clear: letters nested in letters, and the Lord hidden in each as oil is in the seed, the image of 1259.

links.note: The Kural says virtuous action is not killing, and killing brings every other evil deed; Sivavakkiyar says that even one who kills for food, lies and steals may, if he can lovingly join the Lord, know the gods within himself that day. The conflict holds if 1239 makes realisation override the moral law; if it means only that the sinner is not shut out from the Lord, the Kural's ranking of deeds is untouched.

1238 confesses the poet's fear of speaking truth in a world where liars enjoy their lies; 1241 gives the image for it, truth pulled up like a weed among the paddy, and the conclusion that the world of such speakers is hell.

The Kural says a spotless mind is the whole of virtue and all else is noisy show; Sivavakkiyar says those who draw pond water without a drop of moisture in the mind achieve nothing, and that cutting the mind's dirt makes the light, you and I one. Both make the inner state the whole of it.

Tirumular says there are many holy waters within the heart and those who do not bathe in them wander; Sivavakkiyar asks those who pour away water in rites to think of root and seed instead. Both replace the outer bath with an inner object.

Tirumular lists the bathing of the image among the works of the temple that are the servant's path; Sivavakkiyar says those who daily do worship to copper only bewilder themselves, when holding the light within is release. The conflict holds if 1249 condemns image worship as such; if it condemns only image worship in place of inner knowledge, Tirumular's path for the servant stands.

Tirumular says that once the meaning is grasped and samadhi is in hand there is no need of sounded chant or purification; Sivavakkiyar says that holding the measureless light within is release and that muttering and finger-counting are bewilderment. Both make chant redundant for one who has the inner thing.

The Kural speaks of those with impurity in their minds who bathe as if distinguished and go about concealed; Sivavakkiyar says those who dip in the tank do not cut the dirt of the mind. Both charge the bather with a dirty mind under clean water.

Tirumular says the hall where the Lord dances is the whole world, his feet and the five letters; Sivavakkiyar addresses the Lord as the five letters dancing in the sky and the consciousness spread out as sparks. Both make the dance, the mantra and the pervading Lord one thing.

1226 says the eye cannot see itself, so the self within cannot be known; 1258 pushes the image further: the unlookable look, when it comes, looks back at the one looking. Not-knowing in the first verse becomes a reversed seeing in the second.

Both say the Lord is mingled everywhere as a hidden essence is in its substance: Tirumular's jaggery in cane, ghee in milk, juice in fruit and fragrance in flower; Sivavakkiyar's oil in sesame, repeated in 1263 for the Lord hidden in every letter.

Tirumular says there is no dharma outside the Veda and the wise gained release by reciting it; Sivavakkiyar says he has seen no Veda, since he has no burning birth to escape. The conflict holds if 1260 rejects the Veda as a way; if it means only that one already free needs no Veda, Tirumular's claim for those still bound is not denied.

Both contract the mantras: Tirumular's fifty letters, which are all the Vedas and Agamas, become the five letters once their order is known; Sivavakkiyar's five crore mantras are held in the five, and the five, four and three become a single letter within oneself.

Tirumular says the gods go about the eight directions saying 'there he stood, there he lay', while he praises the Lord who dwells within his own heart; Sivavakkiyar calls those who seek the dancing Lord here and there sinners and tells them to seek within. Both set searching in places against finding within.

source_issues: 1240 line 4 repeats line 2 with a variant (அறுவுணர்த்தி for அறிவுணர்த்தி); the unit may have lost its true fourth line.
1250 line 2 has a stray asterisk (*முடரே) for மூடரே.
1263 line 2 (சக்கரத்து சிவ்வைருண்டு சம்புளத் திருந்ததும்) is garbled.
1243 line 4 ஆடுவாழின் is an unclear form.
1252 line 1 வண்டுலங்கள் is an unclear word, perhaps வண்டு (beetle) extended for the rhyme with குண்டலங்கள்.
